doc.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Vladimir Vasiliev, the 500 Club and the Aquarians
summary: Through Herlin Riley he gets a strip-club job on Bourbon Street under Vladimir Vasiliev and joins his Latin band the Aquarians.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: little time under my belt. So that was very inspiring that this guy had a job and I could actually do that. So then I knew I could do it, I was a business major majoring in distributive education, DE. And in DE you had to have a job, because it’s like a management course. So I had a little job at Sears. So I was going to school full time, I was working at Sears plus playing a few little rock gigs here and there, and this guy used to come in and buy fishing equipment. I had no idea who he was. And then one day Herlin Riley, you know him?

The drummer? He and I grew up like brothers. I mean I was the best man in his wedding. And he came in Sears one day and he says, “Hey what are you doing working here, man?” I said, “Well it’s part of my college course and I have to do it.” He says, “Look I’m working a job on Bourbon Street as a trumpet player, but I want the job as the drummer.” He said, “Why don’t you come take this job as the trumpet player?” And I was like, “You play drums?” I didn’t even know he played drums then. He was like, “Yeah.” I said, “Oh come on, man.” He said, “I’m telling you man, I play drums.” So I said okay. So when I went to the audition that night, the guy who was the band leader was this guy who used to come buy the fishing equipment from me. And he was like, “You work at Sears?” I said, “Yeah.” It was such a coincidence. Well it wound up I got that job, it was at the 500 Club, playing for a strip tease show.

And this guy, his name was Vladimir Vasiliev, and he had gone to Berklee in Boston and studied with Margaret Chaloff. Come to find out Lew Soloff was his first trumpet player when Lew was about 19 or 20 years old. And I was telling Lew this story, and he was like, “My God man, I had forgotten about Vladimir.” But that kind of — then I started making a little money and then it was like hey, I could actually make a living doing this. So Vladimir had a great Latin band, which he had like Al McKibbon and Don Alias and Bobby Rodriguez, and all these guys were in his band, Manny Duran. And so we formed a Latin band in New Orleans, The Aquarians was the name of the band. Vladimir and the Aquarians. And then we started growing. He had some beautiful charts that he had written [scats]. Just to play those phrases man was preparing me for futuristic. I didn’t realize it then I was just doing it, I was just making the job. But that was great preparation. Then like I got the call from Papa French and I just kind of played some gigs. In 1979 I played on the New Orleans Jazz Festival with Lionel Hampton. Wallace Davenport was in the band so he called me and he says, “Hey man, can you read?” I said, “Yeah, I can spell a little bit.” So he was like, “Well look, Lionel Hampton needs a trumpet player for the night man, you want to make the job?” So I said yeah.
